visible_observation: The 'Monthly rainfall & flood risk' chart contains a red text label 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' positioned directly over the top of the June and July bars. The text overlaps the bar graphics and the numerical data labels (290, 277) above them.
critique: The placement of the 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' label creates a visual collision that obscures the precise data values for the peak months. This violates the mandate for legibility and precise labels, forcing the viewer to mentally separate the annotation from the data points it is meant to highlight.
revision: Move the 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' text label to the empty white space in the upper-left quadrant of the chart area (above the Jan-Mar bars) and add a thin red arrow or line pointing to the shaded region. Alternatively, place the text in the empty space to the right of the August bar.
protected_strength: The clear visual distinction between 'Lower risk' (light teal) and 'Higher risk' (dark teal) bars, as well as the subtle background shading for the flood window, must be preserved as they effectively communicate the risk hierarchy.
